## Use the Skill locally [#use-the-skill-locally]

Provide the GitHub [`skills/antv-g6lite-graph`](https://github.com/antvis/G6Lite/tree/master/skills/antv-g6lite-graph)
directory as a Skill source to a compatible agent, then invoke it explicitly:

```text
Use $antv-g6lite-graph to build a force-directed dependency graph
with hover highlighting and node dragging.
```

You can also ask an agent to install it directly from GitHub:

```text
Install the skill from
https://github.com/antvis/G6Lite/tree/master/skills/antv-g6lite-graph
```

The Skill keeps the agent focused on these constraints:

* Import only from the `@antv/g6-lite` package root, never `src/` or `dist/` internals.
* Use ESM and a real browser lifecycle with DOM, Canvas, and WebGL.
* Generate only the node, edge, layout, Behavior, Combo, and extension capabilities G6Lite supports.
* Distinguish G6Lite from G6 v5 instead of copying plugin, event, or element configuration.
* For large graphs, examine layout, label density, incremental updates, DPR, GPU, and real devices.

## Good agent tasks [#good-agent-tasks]

| Task                        | Include in the prompt                                            |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create a relationship graph | Data fields, node/edge count, layout, container size             |
| Add interactions            | Selection, drag, tooltip, highlight, brush, or lasso             |
| Migrate from G6 v5          | List capability differences and unsupported needs before editing |
| Diagnose a blank canvas     | Container size, endpoints, WebGL, lifecycle, and version         |
| Optimize a large graph      | First render, layout, labels, state patches, memory, and devices |
| Create an extension         | Category, lifecycle, public ExtensionContext, and cleanup        |

## Recommended workflow [#recommended-workflow]

<div className="ai-workflow not-prose">
  <ol>
    <li>
      <strong>
        Clarify input
      </strong>

      <span>
        Confirm data, scale, coordinates, layout, interactions, and runtime.
      </span>
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>
        Render the minimum
      </strong>

      <span>
        Prove a visible, disposable graph through package-root APIs.
      </span>
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>
        Add layers
      </strong>

      <span>
        Introduce styling, layout, behaviors, states, Combo, and extensions in sequence.
      </span>
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>
        Validate for real
      </strong>

      <span>
        Check the target browser, DPR, GPU, and container dimensions.
      </span>
    </li>
  </ol>
</div>

AI-generated code still needs type checking, browser validation, and product-data review. Do not treat agent output as a production result by itself.

# Changelog (/en/docs/changelog)



G6Lite is currently in the `0.1.0-beta` series. Recent work has concentrated on package-root API boundaries, functional extensions, isolated extension lifecycle, read-only query models, layout cancellation, combo consistency, interaction dispatch, package size governance, examples, and reproducible benchmarks.

## Extension and Behavior contracts — 2026-07-29 [#extension-and-behavior-contracts--2026-07-29]

* Extension is the umbrella term, while Plugin identifies only the peripheral DOM or stateful extension category.
* The public `GraphEventMap`, precise element event types, and typed `Graph.on/off/once` overloads infer known payloads, including zero-argument events and native mouse or wheel events.
* Custom Behaviors use a literal name, `BehaviorOptions`, `BehaviorExtension`, `extensionFactory()`, and an explicit registration function. String references are normalized to `{ type }` before `init()`.
* Behavior handlers are error-isolated with registered-name and event diagnostics. Behavior and Plugin do not promise `update()`; Transform uses it when an instance is reused.
* New English and Chinese Custom Behavior guides document the complete package-author pattern and public capability boundary.

Deprecated beta compatibility APIs remain documented in [API stability](/en/docs/compatibility/api-stability). Projects migrating from G6 v5 should follow the [migration guide](/en/docs/compatibility/g6-v5-migration).

Before upgrading, run type checking, tests, a package build, size-limit, release examples, and target-device validation.


# FAQ (/en/docs/faq)



## Should I use G6Lite or G6 v5? [#should-i-use-g6lite-or-g6-v5]

Choose G6Lite when WebGL rendering, frequent state updates, and a smaller controlled capability surface match the product. Choose G6 v5 when the complete plugin, animation, and element ecosystem matters more.

## Why is first render slow with a force layout? [#why-is-first-render-slow-with-a-force-layout]

Layout computation often dominates first render. Reuse existing coordinates, control iterations, use a worker, or choose a deterministic layout. Measure with the repository Benchmark runner.

## Can G6Lite run during SSR? [#can-g6lite-run-during-ssr]

No. It needs a real DOM canvas and WebGL context. Instantiate `Graph` in a client-only lifecycle such as React `useEffect`.

## Where do TypeScript types come from? [#where-do-typescript-types-come-from]

Import values and types from `@antv/g6-lite`. Deep `src/` paths are not public API.

## Are combos stable? [#are-combos-stable]

Combo rendering is available, but collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping remain experimental in `0.1.x`.


# Overview (/en/docs)



**G6Lite · Lightweight graph visualization, built for large-scale relationship data**

Flexible layouts and interactions, paired with lightweight, efficient WebGL rendering, bring large-scale relationships into focus and make data exploration feel fluid.

Follow the documentation from the first graph to concepts, configuration, examples, reproducible metrics, and compatibility boundaries.

## Core capabilities [#core-capabilities]

* **Lightweight loading** — Keep the core separate from layouts and load algorithms on demand to reduce initial loading overhead.
* **Efficient rendering** — Combine batched WebGL rendering with incremental updates to display and explore large-scale relationship graphs.
* **Flexible layouts and interactions** — Choose from multiple graph layouts and add zoom, pan, drag, selection, and highlighting.
* **Customization and extensions** — Map business data to visual styles and extend graph elements, layouts, and interactions as needed.
* **AI-assisted development** — Use the G6Lite Skill to help an agent create graphs, refine styles, and configure interactions.

## Choosing G6Lite [#choosing-g6lite]

Use G6Lite when WebGL rendering, refresh by change level, built-in layouts, and a controlled extension boundary match your product. If you need the complete G6 plugin and animation ecosystem, evaluate G6 v5 first.


# Extensions (/en/docs/api/extensions)



When configuration cannot express a difference, register it with `register()` and refer to it by name from `GraphOptions`. Tutorials are in [Extensions](/en/docs/guides/extensions), [Custom node](/en/docs/guides/custom-node), and [Custom behavior](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior).

```ts
import { extensionFactory, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';
```

## `register()` [#register]

```ts
register(type, name, extension): void
```

`type` is the extension category. `name` is the string later written into configuration, and it cannot be empty. A later registration with the same category and name replaces the previous definition.

| `type`         | Where the name is used                       | What the extension provides                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'node'`       | `node.type`                                  | `base?: 'circle' \| 'rect'`, default `style`, `stateStyles`, and `getStyle(node)`. Optional `drawOverlay()` draws a screen-space decoration, and `getBoundaryAnchor()` returns a point on the node boundary |
| `'edge'`       | `edge.type`                                  | `base?: 'line' \| 'arc' \| 'polyline' \| 'cubic'`, default `style`, `stateStyles`, and `getStyle(source, target, edge)`                                                                                     |
| `'label'`      | `node.labelRenderer` or `edge.labelRenderer` | `measure(params)` returns width and height; `draw(params)` paints onto the canvas                                                                                                                           |
| `'decoration'` | `node.decorations[].renderer`                | The same `measure` / `draw` pair, with data from the decoration config                                                                                                                                      |
| `'layout'`     | `layout.type`                                | `execute(data, context)` returns nodes with `x` and `y`. `context` includes `width`, `height`, `signal`, and the current `options`                                                                          |
| `'behavior'`   | `type` inside `behaviors`                    | `getEvents()` maps event names to handlers. Implement `init(context, options)` and `destroy()` when the behavior has a lifecycle                                                                            |
| `'transform'`  | `type` inside `transforms`                   | `beforeRender(data)` returns the next `GraphData`. Implement `update(options)` when options can change                                                                                                      |
| `'plugin'`     | `type` inside `plugins`                      | `mount(container)` attaches independent DOM. Use `init` / `destroy` for its lifecycle                                                                                                                       |

Node and edge extensions are usually stateless style objects. Layouts, behaviors, transforms, and plugins usually keep state, so wrap them in `extensionFactory()`.

```ts
register('edge', 'dependency', {
  base: 'arc',
  style: { stroke: '#91caff', curvature: 0.2, endArrow: true },
});

register(
  'behavior',
  'pin-click',
  extensionFactory(() => {
    let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;
    return {
      init(next) {
        context = next;
      },
      getEvents() {
        return {
          'node:click': ({ nodeId }) => context?.state.set(nodeId, ['selected']),
        };
      },
    };
  }),
);
```

Register before creating the Graph, or before a render that reads the name. Behaviors, transforms, and plugins resolve names from the registry at render time.

A plain object or a zero-argument class can still be registered. Objects are cloned on a best-effort basis, and classes are constructed again. Use `extensionFactory()` when a stateful extension needs a predictable instance per graph.

## `extensionFactory()` [#extensionfactory]

```ts
extensionFactory(factory: () => Extension): () => Extension
```

Marks the function as an extension factory. The engine calls it once per Graph, so graphs do not share one closure.

## Extension context [#extension-context]

Behaviors, plugins, and some layouts receive `ExtensionContext` from `init(context, options)`. `options` is read-only.

| Member                                                       | Use                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `context.data.getNode(id)` / `getEdge(id)`                   | Read a read-only snapshot                   |
| `context.data.getNodeIds()` / `getEdgeIds()`                 | Current id lists                            |
| `context.data.updateNode(id, data)` / `updateEdge(id, data)` | Merge business fields                       |
| `context.state.set(id, states)`                              | Replace one element's state list            |
| `context.state.setAll(stateMap)`                             | Replace many elements at once               |
| `context.state.get(id)` / `clear(id)`                        | Read or clear state                         |
| `context.viewport.screenToGraph(point)`                      | Client coordinates to graph coordinates     |
| `context.viewport.graphToScreen(point)`                      | Graph coordinates to client coordinates     |
| `context.viewport.getZoom()`                                 | Current zoom                                |
| `context.requestRender()`                                    | Request a draw on the next frame            |
| `context.isDestroyed()`                                      | Whether the owning Graph has been destroyed |

Snapshots from `data` cannot be mutated in place. Write through `updateNode`, `updateEdge`, and `state`.

`context.graph`, and the flat `screenToGraph()`, `graphToScreen()`, and `getZoom()` on the context, remain for existing extensions. New extensions use `data`, `state`, `viewport`, and `requestRender()`.

## `runLayout()` [#runlayout]

Compute positions without creating a Graph:

```ts
import { runLayout } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const result = await runLayout(
  { nodes, edges },
  { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR' },
  { width: 800, height: 600 },
);

result.nodes.forEach((node) => {
  node.x;
  node.y;
});
```

```ts
runLayout(
  data: GraphData,
  config: LayoutConfig,
  viewport?: { width: number; height: number },
): Promise<LayoutResult>
```

`LayoutResult` is `{ nodes }`, and every node has numeric `x` and `y`. A registered layout of the same name, and the built-in `mindmap`, `indented`, and `fishbone` layouts, run before `@antv/layout`. With `config.worker: true`, algorithms that support a Worker run there and fall back to the same algorithm on the main thread if the Worker fails.

To rerun layout on a Graph that is already rendered, use [`graph.setLayout()`](/en/docs/api/graph#layout) and `graph.layout()`. Those calls write coordinates back into the current graph and draw.


# Graph (/en/docs/api/graph)



`Graph` is the instance application code uses to operate one graph. Import it from the package root, pass [options](/en/docs/api/options), then `await graph.render()`.

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({ container, data });
await graph.render();
```

Data writes, state changes, and `layout()` run after the first successful `render()`. After `destroy()`, those methods return immediately.

## Lifecycle [#lifecycle]

### `new Graph(options)` [#new-graphoptions]

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: document.getElementById('container')!,
  data: { nodes: [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }], edges: [{ source: 'a', target: 'b' }] },
});
```

Stores `container`, `data`, and the rest of the configuration, then creates a canvas inside the container. There is no layout result yet, and element queries are empty.

`container` accepts a CSS selector (such as `#container`) or an `HTMLElement`. The element must already be in the document.

### `render()` [#render]

```ts
await graph.render();
```

Runs the configured transforms and layout, initializes the runtime, and draws the first frame. Wait for the first render before calling data and state methods. See [Graph lifecycle](/en/docs/concepts/graph-lifecycle) for initialization and asynchronous cleanup.

Calling it again on the same instance cancels an in-flight layout and redraws from the latest data and options.

The render emits `beforerender` and `afterrender`.

### `destroy()` [#destroy]

```ts
graph.destroy();
```

Aborts an in-flight layout, emits `destroy`, tears down interactions, plugins, and the renderer, and removes the canvas. A second call has no further effect. `destroyed` is then `true`.

### `destroyed` [#destroyed]

```ts
if (graph.destroyed) return;
```

Whether the instance has been destroyed.

### `refresh()` [#refresh]

```ts
graph.refresh();
```

Forces one full style pass and draw. Data, state, and viewport changes already schedule their own frame. Call this only when an input changed outside the methods the engine observes.

## Reading data [#reading-data]

Queries return the current read-only view. Use the write methods below to change what is drawn.

```ts
const snapshot = graph.getData();
const nodes = graph.getNodes();
const node = graph.getNodeData('n1');
const neighbors = graph.getNeighborNodes('n1');
const edges = graph.getAdjacentEdges('n1');

if (graph.hasNode('n1') && node) {
  node.x;
  node.y;
  node.data;
  neighbors.length;
  edges[0]?.source;
  snapshot.nodes.length;
}
```

| Method                     | Returns                     | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getData()`                | `GraphData`                 | Snapshot of the current nodes, edges, and combos                  |
| `getNodes()`               | `readonly NodeModel[]`      | Every node                                                        |
| `getNodeData(id)`          | `NodeModel \| undefined`    | Node by id                                                        |
| `getEdges()`               | `readonly EdgeModel[]`      | Every edge                                                        |
| `getEdgeData(id)`          | `EdgeModel \| undefined`    | Edge by id                                                        |
| `getComboData(id)`         | `ComboModel \| undefined`   | Combo by id                                                       |
| `getElementData(id)`       | `ElementModel \| undefined` | Node, edge, or combo by id                                        |
| `getNodeCount()`           | `number`                    | Node count                                                        |
| `getEdgeCount()`           | `number`                    | Edge count                                                        |
| `hasNode(id)`              | `boolean`                   | Whether the node exists                                           |
| `hasEdge(id)`              | `boolean`                   | Whether the edge exists                                           |
| `hasElement(id)`           | `boolean`                   | Whether that node, edge, or combo exists                          |
| `getElementPosition(id)`   | `{ x, y } \| null`          | Graph position of a node or combo. An edge has no single position |
| `getNeighborNodes(nodeId)` | `string[]`                  | Ids of neighboring nodes                                          |
| `getAdjacentEdges(nodeId)` | `{ id, source, target }[]`  | Edges connected to the node                                       |

`NodeModel` has `id`, `name`, `x`, `y`, `data`, and `states`. `EdgeModel` has `id`, `source`, `target`, `data`, and `states`. `states` is a read-only set.

Before the first `render()`, `getData()` returns a copy of the data passed to the constructor. The other queries behave as an empty graph.

## Replacing data and styles [#replacing-data-and-styles]

### `setData()` [#setdata]

```ts
await graph.setData(
  {
    nodes: [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  { fitView: false },
);
```

Replaces the whole graph with a new set of nodes, edges, and combos. A configured `layout` runs again, the graph redraws, and `datachange` is emitted.

`options.fitView` controls the viewport after replacement:

* Omitted or `true`: calls `fitView()` with `0.9`.
* `false`: keeps the current camera.
* A number or `FitViewOptions`: forwards that value to `fitView()`.

Use the incremental methods below for local additions and edits so the whole graph is not laid out again.

### `updateOptions()` [#updateoptions]

```ts
graph.updateOptions({
  node: { style: { fill: '#5366ad', size: 32 } },
  theme: { type: 'light' },
});
```

Merges node, edge, label, and theme options, then recomputes styles. Object `style` values merge with the previous style. A function style replaces the previous style entirely.

Layout, behaviors, and plugins are outside this argument. Change layout with `setLayout()` followed by `layout()`.

## Changing nodes and edges [#changing-nodes-and-edges]

These methods require a completed first `render()`. Batch methods draw once.

### Nodes [#nodes]

```ts
graph.addNode({ id: 'n4', x: 240, y: 80, data: { label: 'N4' } });
graph.updateNodeData('n4', { label: 'Updated' });
graph.updateNodePosition('n4', 260, 100);
graph.updateNodePositions([
  { id: 'n1', x: 40, y: 40 },
  { id: 'n4', x: 280, y: 120 },
]);
graph.removeNode('n4');
```

`addNode()` requires a unique `id` and graph coordinates. It does not run layout again.

`updateNodeData()` merges the business payload. Style functions that read those fields are recomputed on the next frame.

`removeNode()` also removes edges connected to that node.

A successful change emits `afteradditem`, `afterupdateitem`, or `afterremoveitem`.

### Edges [#edges]

```ts
const edgeId = graph.addEdge({ source: 'n1', target: 'n4', data: { weight: 1 } });
graph.updateEdgeData(edgeId, { weight: 2 });
graph.updateEdgeData([{ id: edgeId, source: 'n2', target: 'n4' }]);
graph.removeEdge(edgeId);
```

`source` and `target` must already exist. When `id` is omitted the engine generates one, and the return value is that id. Later queries and removal use it.

The batch form of `updateEdgeData()` can also change an edge's endpoints.

## State, visibility, and focus [#state-visibility-and-focus]

Built-in state names are `default`, `active`, `selected`, `disabled`, `highlight`, `inactive`, and `hidden`. Application-defined names are accepted and can be styled with `node.stateStyles` or `edge.stateStyles`.

### `setItemState()` [#setitemstate]

```ts
graph.setItemState('n1', 'selected', true);
graph.setItemState('n1', 'selected', false);
```

Turns one state on or off for a node, edge, or combo. `value: false` removes only that state.

### `setElementStates()` [#setelementstates]

```ts
graph.setElementStates('n1', ['selected', 'highlight']);
graph.setElementStates({
  n1: ['selected'],
  'a-b': ['active'],
});
```

Replaces the complete state list of an element. The object form updates many elements and draws once.

### `batchSetState()` [#batchsetstate]

```ts
graph.batchSetState([
  { id: 'n1', state: 'highlight', value: true },
  { id: 'n2', state: 'inactive', value: true },
]);
```

Turns individual states on or off in one batch. Use it when one interaction, such as hover highlight, touches many elements.

### Query and clear [#query-and-clear]

```ts
const states = graph.getItemStates('n1');
const selected = graph.findNodesByState('selected');
graph.clearItemStates('n1');
```

`clearItemStates()` removes every state on that element. The `find*ByState()` methods return ids that currently have the state.

### `hideItem()` and `showItem()` [#hideitem-and-showitem]

```ts
graph.hideItem('n2');
graph.showItem('n2');
```

Hide or show a node, edge, or combo through the `hidden` state. `showItem()` clears only `hidden` and leaves other states in place.

### `focusItem()` [#focusitem]

```ts
graph.focusItem('n1');
graph.focusItem(['n1', 'n2'], 24);
```

Centers the viewport on one or more nodes. The current zoom is kept when the targets fit. Otherwise the view zooms out just enough to leave `padding` screen pixels. The default `padding` is `20`. Nothing happens when none of the ids resolve to a node.

## Viewport [#viewport]

The camera is the current view: graph-space translation `x` and `y`, plus `zoom`.

```ts
const camera = graph.getCamera();
graph.setCamera({ x: camera.x, y: camera.y, zoom: 1 });
graph.zoomBy(1.2);
graph.fitCenter();
graph.resetCamera();
```

| Method                   | Description                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getCamera()`            | Returns a `{ x, y, zoom }` snapshot                                                     |
| `setCamera(partial)`     | Merges the provided camera fields                                                       |
| `resetCamera()`          | Returns to the camera captured at the end of the first render. Earlier calls do nothing |
| `getZoom()`              | Current zoom                                                                            |
| `setSize(width, height)` | Sets the canvas size in CSS pixels                                                      |
| `fitCenter()`            | Keeps zoom and moves the graph content to the viewport center                           |

### Container resize [#container-resize]

Graph uses `ResizeObserver` to synchronize the canvas with its container. `setSize(width, height)` updates canvas dimensions in CSS pixels through the same viewport update path.

By default, resizing preserves the current camera so the user's zoom and pan remain intact. Enabling [`autoFit`](/en/docs/api/options#autofit) fits the content again according to that configuration.

The `resize` event fires after optional fitting, so listeners observe the final camera. A size change does not require a new instance or another `render()`.

### `zoomTo()` and `zoomBy()` [#zoomto-and-zoomby]

```ts
graph.zoomTo(1.5, { center: { x: 320, y: 180 } });
graph.zoomBy(2, { minZoom: 0.2, maxZoom: 8 });
```

`zoomTo()` sets an absolute zoom. `zoomBy(2)` multiplies the current zoom by 2.

`ZoomOptions`:

| Field     | Default                                | Description                                 |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `center`  | Client coordinate of the canvas center | Screen point that stays fixed while zooming |
| `minZoom` | `0.1`                                  | Lower zoom bound                            |
| `maxZoom` | `20`                                   | Upper zoom bound                            |

### `fitView()` [#fitview]

```ts
graph.fitView();
graph.fitView(0.8);
graph.fitView({ padding: [24, 16, 24, 16], minZoom: 0.2, maxZoom: 2 });
```

Fits the camera to the bounding box of every node.

* A number is a scale applied to that fit. The default is `0.9`. The first `render()` uses it unless [`autoFit`](/en/docs/api/options#autofit) supplies another policy.
* An object uses `padding`, `minZoom`, and `maxZoom`. `padding` is one CSS pixel value or `[top, right, bottom, left]`. The scale is `1`, `minZoom` defaults to `0.1`, and `maxZoom` defaults to `20`.

### Coordinate conversion [#coordinate-conversion]

```ts
graph.on('canvas:click', (event) => {
  const point = graph.screenToGraph(event.nativeEvent.clientX, event.nativeEvent.clientY);
  const screen = graph.graphToScreen(point.x, point.y);
  screen.x;
});
```

Arguments and return values are client coordinates, the same space as `MouseEvent.clientX` and `clientY`. Element events already split `client`, `canvas`, and `graph`, so most click handlers can read those fields directly.

## Layout [#layout]

```ts
graph.setLayout({ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR' });
await graph.layout();
graph.cancelLayout();
```

`setLayout()` replaces the layout used by the next run. `layout()` executes it on the current graph data and writes the resulting coordinates back to the nodes. It returns immediately when no layout is configured or the graph has no nodes.

`cancelLayout()` abandons an in-flight layout. An older run that finishes later does not overwrite a newer result.

Layout names and parameters are in [Layout](/en/docs/guides/layout). To compute positions without a Graph, use [`runLayout()`](/en/docs/api/extensions#runlayout).

## Combo [#combo]

Combo collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping are experimental. Their configuration may change within `0.1.x`. Visual options are in [Combo](/en/docs/guides/combo). Call these methods after the first `render()`. A call before that returns immediately and does not create or change a combo.

```ts
graph.createCombo({ id: 'group', data: { label: 'Group' } }, ['n1', 'n2']);
graph.addToCombo('n3', 'group');
const children = graph.getComboChildren('group');
graph.collapseCombo('group');
graph.expandCombo('group');
graph.removeFromCombo('n3');
graph.removeCombo('group');
children.nodes;
```

The second argument of `createCombo()` places existing nodes into the new combo. `collapseCombo()` hides the nodes under it and emits `combo:collapse`. `expandCombo()` restores them and emits `combo:expand`. Collapsing or expanding a combo that is already in the target state does not emit again.

Select and hide combos with `setItemState()` and `hideItem()`. The older `setComboState()` remains only for existing code.

## Events [#events]

```ts
graph.once('afterrender', () => {
  graph.fitView(0.9);
});
```

Names in `GraphEventMap` infer the handler argument. Custom event names can be subscribed too; the handler declares that payload.

```ts
graph.on('node:click', (event) => {
  event.nodeId;
  event.nativeEvent.clientX;
});

const onRender = (payload: { nodeCount: number; edgeCount: number }) => {
  console.log(payload.nodeCount);
};
graph.on('afterrender', onRender);
graph.off('afterrender', onRender);
```

`off()` needs the same function that was passed to `on()`. `once()` removes the listener after the first emit. `destroy` has no arguments.

Element click, hover, and wheel events are emitted by the engine and do not require an extra behavior. Selection, drag, brush, and lasso events appear only when that behavior is enabled. Field notes are in [Events](/en/docs/guides/events).

| Event                                                      | Main fields                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `node:*`                                                   | `nodeId`, `nativeEvent`, `data`, `graph`                  |
| `edge:*`                                                   | `edgeId`, `edgeIndex`, `source`, `target`, `nativeEvent`  |
| `combo:pointerdown` / `click` / `dblclick` / `contextmenu` | `comboId`, `nativeEvent`                                  |
| `canvas:*`                                                 | `nativeEvent`, and no target element id                   |
| `node:selectchange`                                        | `nodeId`, `selected`, `event`                             |
| `edge:selectchange`                                        | `edgeId`, `edgeIndex`, `source`, `target`, `selected`     |
| `selection:clear`                                          | `ids`                                                     |
| `node:dragstart` / `node:drag` / `node:dragend`            | `nodeId`, `nodeIds`; drag also has `dx`, `dy`             |
| `combo:dragstart` / `combo:drag` / `combo:dragend`         | `comboId`; drag also has `dx`, `dy`                       |
| `edge:dragstart` / `edge:drag` / `edge:dragend`            | `source`, `target`, `dragEnd`; end also has `reconnected` |
| `brush:select` / `brush:end`                               | `nodeIds`                                                 |
| `lasso:select` / `lasso:end`                               | `nodeIds`                                                 |
| `beforelayout` / `layout:start`                            | `nodeCount`                                               |
| `layout:end` / `afterlayout`                               | `duration`, `nodeCount`                                   |
| `beforerender` / `afterrender`                             | `nodeCount`, `edgeCount`                                  |
| `resize`                                                   | `width`, `height`                                         |
| `datachange`                                               | `nodeCount`, `edgeCount`                                  |
| `afteradditem`                                             | `type`, `id`; edges also include `source`, `target`       |
| `afterremoveitem`                                          | `type`, `id`                                              |
| `afterupdateitem`                                          | `type`, `id`, `action`                                    |
| `combo:collapse` / `combo:expand`                          | `comboId`                                                 |
| `destroy`                                                  | No arguments                                              |

`node:*` and `edge:*` each include `pointerover`, `pointerenter`, `pointermove`, `pointerleave`, `pointerdown`, `click`, `dblclick`, `contextmenu`, and `wheel`. `canvas:*` includes `pointermove`, `pointerdown`, `pointerup`, `click`, `dblclick`, `contextmenu`, and `wheel`.

The native input is `nativeEvent`. The older `event` field remains for existing listeners.


# Usable APIs (/en/docs/api)



Application code imports only from the `@antv/g6-lite` package root. This page lists the functions, classes, and types you can call directly. Configuration recipes, interaction examples, and extension tutorials stay in the guides.

```ts
import { Graph, register, extensionFactory, runLayout, resolveTheme } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import type {
  GraphData,
  GraphOptions,
  GraphEventMap,
  NodeModel,
  ElementState,
} from '@antv/g6-lite';
```

The package is ESM-only. A CommonJS app crosses the client boundary with a dynamic import:

```js
const { Graph } = await import('@antv/g6-lite');
```

`Graph` needs a real DOM, Canvas, and WebGL context. It cannot be constructed in an environment without a canvas.

## Call order [#call-order]

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: document.getElementById('container')!,
  data: { nodes: [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }], edges: [{ source: 'a', target: 'b' }] },
  layout: { type: 'force' },
});

graph.on('node:click', (event) => {
  graph.setItemState(event.nodeId, 'selected', true);
});

await graph.render();

graph.destroy();
```

`new Graph()` stores the options and prepares the canvas. Layout, drawing, and later data changes wait for `await graph.render()`. Calling `setData()`, `addNode()`, `setItemState()`, or `layout()` before that throws `Graph must be rendered before calling data operations`.

Queries before the first render describe an empty graph: `getNodes()` is `[]` and `getNodeData()` is `undefined`. `graph.on()` can be registered before `render()`.

## Entries you can call [#entries-you-can-call]

| Entry                                                                | Use                                                                                        | Reference                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `Graph`                                                              | Create a graph, read and write data, set state, control the viewport, and listen to events | [Graph](/en/docs/api/graph)           |
| `GraphOptions` and the node, edge, layout, behavior, and theme types | Declare the initial configuration                                                          | [Options](/en/docs/api/options)       |
| `register()`                                                         | Register a custom node, edge, label, decoration, layout, behavior, transform, or plugin    | [Extensions](/en/docs/api/extensions) |
| `extensionFactory()`                                                 | Give a stateful extension its own instance on every Graph                                  | [Extensions](/en/docs/api/extensions) |
| `runLayout()`                                                        | Compute node positions without creating a Graph                                            | [Extensions](/en/docs/api/extensions) |
| `resolveTheme()`                                                     | Turn `'light'`, `'dark'`, or a partial token object into a complete `ThemeTokens`          | [Options](/en/docs/api/options)       |

These types are also exported from the package root: `GraphData`, `GraphNode`, `GraphEdge`, `ComboData`, `NodeModel`, `EdgeModel`, `ComboModel`, `ElementState`, `GraphEventMap`, `FitViewOptions`, `ZoomOptions`, `SetDataOptions`, `LayoutConfig`, `LabelOptions`, `ThemeOption`, and `BehaviorOption`.

## Query results are read-only [#query-results-are-read-only]

`getNodeData()`, `getEdgeData()`, and `getComboData()` return read-only views. Change position, payload, and state through the write methods:

```ts
const node = graph.getNodeData('a');
if (node) {
  graph.updateNodeData(node.id, { ...node.data, highlighted: true });
  graph.updateNodePosition(node.id, node.x + 20, node.y);
  graph.setItemState(node.id, 'selected', true);
}
```

Assigning `node.x`, or calling `node.states.add()`, does not update the canvas. The type checker rejects those writes.

## Engine-only members [#engine-only-members]

These `Graph` members exist for rendering and interaction dispatch. Application code uses the public entry in the right column.

| Engine member                         | Application entry                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `eventEmitter`                        | `graph.on()` / `graph.off()` / `graph.once()`       |
| `getCanvas()`                         | The canvas DOM stays inside the engine              |
| `getLayoutNodes()` / `getNodeIndex()` | `getNodes()` / `getNodeData()`                      |
| `pickAt()` / `pickComboAt()`          | `nodeId`, `edgeId`, and `comboId` on element events |
| `setHighlight()` / `clearHighlight()` | `setItemState()` with the `highlight` state         |
| `updateData()` / `scheduleRender()`   | The data methods and `refresh()`                    |

`EventEmitter` and `Handler` are exported as the event-transport types. Subscribe to graph events with `graph.on()`.

## Compatibility entries [#compatibility-entries]

New code uses the current entry. The symbols below can still be imported and will be removed according to [API stability](/en/docs/compatibility/api-stability).

| Compatibility entry                                           | Current entry                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BaseNode`, `BreathingNode`, `registerNode()`                 | `register('node', name, extension)`                        |
| `graph.isDestroyed()`                                         | `graph.destroyed`                                          |
| `graph.toData()`                                              | `graph.getData()`                                          |
| `graph.getNodePosition()`                                     | `graph.getElementPosition()`                               |
| `setComboState()` / `clearComboStates()` / `getComboStates()` | `setItemState()` / `clearItemStates()` / `getItemStates()` |
| Event field `event`                                           | `nativeEvent`                                              |
| `context.graph` and the flat coordinate methods               | `context.data`, `context.state`, `context.viewport`        |


# Options (/en/docs/api/options)



The argument of `new Graph(options)` is `GraphOptions`. Only `container` and `data` are required. Node appearance, edge appearance, layout, interaction, and theme all have defaults and can be overridden where the graph needs to differ.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  node: { style: { size: 28, fill: '#5366ad' } },
  edge: { style: { endArrow: true } },
  layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'TB' },
  behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'click-select'],
  theme: 'light',
});
```

Visual recipes live in the guides: [Data](/en/docs/guides/data), [Node](/en/docs/guides/node), [Edge](/en/docs/guides/edge), [Label](/en/docs/guides/label), [Layout](/en/docs/guides/layout), [Interactions](/en/docs/guides/interactions), and [Theme](/en/docs/guides/theme).

## GraphOptions [#graphoptions]

| Field        | Type                                  | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container`  | `string \| HTMLElement`               | Canvas container. A string is a CSS selector, such as `#container`                                  |
| `data`       | `GraphData`                           | Nodes, edges, and optional combos                                                                   |
| `node`       | `NodeConfig`                          | Node shape, style, and state styles                                                                 |
| `edge`       | `EdgeConfig`                          | Edge shape, style, arrows, and state styles                                                         |
| `combo`      | `ComboConfig`                         | Combo appearance. Collapse and nesting are still experimental                                       |
| `label`      | `LabelOptions`                        | Zoom and collision policy shared by node and edge labels                                            |
| `layout`     | `LayoutConfig`                        | Layout type and algorithm parameters                                                                |
| `behaviors`  | `BehaviorOption[]`                    | Interaction list. Omitted means wheel zoom and drag pan                                             |
| `transforms` | `TransformOption[]`                   | Data transforms before drawing, such as parallel edges                                              |
| `plugins`    | `PluginOption[]`                      | Registered plugins                                                                                  |
| `theme`      | `ThemeOption`                         | `'light'`, `'dark'`, or a preset plus token overrides                                               |
| `autoFit`    | `boolean \| number \| FitViewOptions` | Whether a container resize calls `fitView()` again. Default `false`, which keeps the current camera |

See [`autoFit`](#autofit) below for initial fitting and resize fitting.

At runtime, `node`, `edge`, `label`, and `theme` can be updated with [`graph.updateOptions()`](/en/docs/api/graph#updateoptions).

### `autoFit` [#autofit]

Controls initial fitting and whether a container resize fits the graph again:

| Value                        | First `render()`       | After resize                    |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Omitted or `false` (default) | `fitView(0.9)`         | Preserve the current camera     |
| `true`                       | `fitView(0.9)`         | `fitView(0.9)`                  |
| `FitViewOptions` object      | Fit with those options | Fit again with the same options |

A positive number supplies the relative scale for `fitView()`, both during the initial render and after resizing.

For resizable panels or expanding sidebars, an options object can control the fit:

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: '#container',
  data,
  autoFit: { padding: 24, minZoom: 0.2, maxZoom: 1.5 },
});
```

See [`fitView()`](/en/docs/api/graph#fitview) for `padding`, `minZoom`, and `maxZoom`. Leave automatic fitting disabled to preserve the user's zoom and pan. Disabling it affects only resize fitting; the initial render still fits the graph.

See [Container resize](/en/docs/api/graph#container-resize) for observation and event ordering.

## Graph data [#graph-data]

```ts
const data: GraphData = {
  nodes: [{ id: 'a', data: { cluster: 'svc' } }, { id: 'b' }],
  edges: [{ source: 'a', target: 'b', data: { weight: 1 } }],
  combos: [{ id: 'group', collapsed: false }],
};
```

### Node `GraphNode` [#node-graphnode]

| Field       | Required | Description                                                                            |
| ----------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | Yes      | Unique in the graph                                                                    |
| `name`      | No       | Node name                                                                              |
| `data`      | No       | Business fields. Style functions and tooltips read them here                           |
| `x` / `y`   | No       | Existing coordinates, used when there is no layout or as the layout's initial position |
| `fx` / `fy` | No       | Coordinates fixed during layout                                                        |
| `states`    | No       | Initial states, such as `['selected']`                                                 |
| `comboId`   | No       | Id of the owning combo                                                                 |

### Edge `GraphEdge` [#edge-graphedge]

| Field    | Required | Description                          |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `source` | Yes      | Source node id                       |
| `target` | Yes      | Target node id                       |
| `id`     | No       | Generated by the engine when omitted |
| `data`   | No       | Business fields                      |
| `states` | No       | Initial states                       |

### Combo `ComboData` [#combo-combodata]

| Field       | Description                             |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | Required and unique                     |
| `parentId`  | Parent combo, used for nesting          |
| `collapsed` | Whether it starts collapsed             |
| `style`     | Style overrides on top of `combo.style` |
| `data`      | Business fields                         |
| `states`    | Initial states                          |

## Node [#node]

```ts
node?: {
  type?: 'circle' | 'rect' | string;
  labelRenderer?: string;
  decorations?: NodeDecorationConfig[];
  autoExternalLabelPlacement?: boolean;
  style?: NodeStyleConfig | ((node: GraphNode) => Partial<NodeStyleConfig>);
  stateStyles?: Partial<Record<ElementState, NodeStateStyleOverride>>;
}
```

An omitted `type`, or `'circle'`, draws a circle. `'rect'` draws a rounded rectangle. Any other string must already be registered with `register('node', ...)`.

Each visual field in `style` can be a constant or `(node: GraphNode) => value`. `label: false` and `icon: false` skip that layer.

| Style field                                                                  | Description                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fill` / `stroke` / `strokeWidth` / `opacity`                                | Fill, stroke, and opacity                                                                       |
| `size`                                                                       | Circle diameter, or the size used when width and height are not set separately                  |
| `width` / `height` / `borderRadius`                                          | Rectangle size and corner radius                                                                |
| `label`                                                                      | Text, or a function that returns text. Omitted means no node label; `false` explicitly hides it |
| `labelFontSize` / `labelFontFamily` / `labelFontWeight` / `labelColor`       | Text appearance                                                                                 |
| `labelPlacement`                                                             | `'center' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right'`, default `'bottom'`                        |
| `labelOffsetX` / `labelOffsetY`                                              | Offset from the placement point                                                                 |
| `labelBackground` / `labelBackgroundPadding` / `labelMaxWidth`               | Text background, padding, and maximum width                                                     |
| `icon` / `iconType`                                                          | Icon content. `iconType` is `'image'` or `'text'`                                               |
| `iconWidth` / `iconHeight` / `iconFontFamily` / `iconFontSize` / `iconColor` | Icon size and text-icon style                                                                   |
| `iconOffsetX` / `iconOffsetY`                                                | Icon offset                                                                                     |

`stateStyles` overrides `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `opacity`, and `haloWidth` while that state is active. Turn states on and off with the [Graph state methods](/en/docs/api/graph#state-visibility-and-focus).

`labelRenderer` is the name of a registered custom label renderer. `decorations` attaches badges and other node decorations; register the renderer with `register('decoration', ...)`. Fields and collision rules are in [Label](/en/docs/guides/label) and [Custom node](/en/docs/guides/custom-node).

## Edge [#edge]

```ts
edge?: {
  type?: 'line' | 'arc' | 'polyline' | 'cubic' | string;
  labelRenderer?: string;
  parallelEdges?: boolean | ParallelEdgesConfig;
  style?: { /* fields below; values may be functions */ };
  stateStyles?: Partial<Record<ElementState, EdgeStateStyleOverride>>;
}
```

An edge style function is `(source, target, edge) => value`.

| Style field                                                      | Description                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stroke` / `lineWidth` / `opacity` / `lineDash`                  | Color, width, opacity, and dash pattern                                          |
| `hitAreaWidth`                                                   | Pickable width in screen pixels. Defaults to the final line width                |
| `curvature` / `curveOffset`                                      | Bend of arcs and curves                                                          |
| `endArrow` / `startArrow` / `arrowSize`                          | End arrow, start arrow, and size                                                 |
| `radius`                                                         | Polyline corner radius                                                           |
| `router`                                                         | Polyline routing: `'orth' \| 'tree' \| 'indented' \| 'fishbone'`                 |
| `label`, plus `labelFontSize`, `labelFontFamily`, `labelColor`   | Edge label content. Omitted `label` draws nothing; the default font size is `10` |
| `labelPlacement`                                                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                                                   |
| `labelBackground` / `labelBackgroundPadding` / `labelAutoRotate` | Background, padding, and whether the text follows the edge                       |

`stateStyles` can override `stroke`, `lineWidth`, `hitAreaWidth`, `opacity`, and `lineDash`.

`parallelEdges: true` separates edges that share endpoints with the default spacing. The object form is:

| Field            | Default       | Description                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`        | on            | Whether separation runs                       |
| `offset`         | `20`          | Graph-space distance between adjacent edges   |
| `mergeBy`        | source/target | Grouping currently supports the two endpoints |
| `includeReverse` | `true`        | `A→B` and `B→A` belong to one group           |
| `minOffset`      | `0`           | Minimum absolute offset for non-center edges  |
| `maxOffset`      | `80`          | Maximum absolute offset                       |

`'process-parallel-edges'` in `transforms` has the same effect. See [Parallel edges](/en/docs/guides/parallel-edges).

## Label policy [#label-policy]

`label` controls how the engine shows node and edge labels that already have text. It does not choose the text.

| Field             | Default | Description                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scaleWithZoom`   | `true`  | Whether node-label size follows camera zoom. Edge labels stay in screen space |
| `hideOnLowZoom`   | `true`  | Hide labels below their zoom threshold                                        |
| `hideOnCollision` | `true`  | Hide a label that overlaps an earlier one                                     |
| `nodeMinZoom`     | `0.3`   | Minimum zoom for node labels                                                  |
| `edgeMinZoom`     | `0.5`   | Minimum zoom for edge labels                                                  |

## Layout [#layout]

```ts
layout?: {
  type: string;
  worker?: boolean;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  center?: [number, number];
  [algorithmOption: string]: unknown;
}
```

`type` is a built-in name or a registered layout name, such as `'force'`, `'dagre'`, or `'mindmap'`. The remaining fields are passed to that algorithm. `worker: true` runs supported algorithms in a Web Worker. Omitted `width`, `height`, and `center` are derived from the canvas.

Available types, parameters, and rerunning layout are in [Layout](/en/docs/guides/layout).

## Interactions [#interactions]

Each `behaviors` item is a behavior name or `{ type, ...options }`.

Omitting the field is equivalent to `['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas']`. Once an array is passed, that array is the complete list. `[]` turns off the default zoom and pan.

| `type`            | Effect                                                                         | Options                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zoom-canvas`     | Wheel zoom                                                                     | `sensitivity` default `1`, `minZoom` default `0.1`, `maxZoom` default `20`              |
| `drag-canvas`     | Drag to pan                                                                    | `ignoreModifierKeys` default `true`, so a modifier key stays available for brush select |
| `drag-node`       | Drag a node                                                                    | No extra options                                                                        |
| `drag-edge`       | Drag an edge endpoint to reconnect it                                          | No extra options                                                                        |
| `click-select`    | Click to select a node or edge                                                 | `multiple` default `false`; `trigger` default `'shift'`, also `'ctrl'` or `'meta'`      |
| `hover-highlight` | Highlight a neighborhood on hover                                              | `degree` default `1`; optional `inactiveState`                                          |
| `highlight-node`  | Hovering a node highlights it, its one-hop neighbors, and the connecting edges | No extra options                                                                        |
| `highlight-edge`  | Hovering an edge highlights it and its endpoints                               | No extra options                                                                        |
| `brush-select`    | Rectangular selection                                                          | `key` is `'shift'`, `'ctrl'`, or `null`; `throttleMs` default `100`                     |
| `lasso-select`    | Freeform selection                                                             | Same options as `brush-select`                                                          |
| `tooltip`         | Overlay                                                                        | See the table below                                                                     |

`tooltip` options:

| Field        | Default                        | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`    | `'hover'`                      | `'hover'` or `'click'`                                                                                                    |
| `getContent` | Node id, or the edge endpoints | Returns a string or `HTMLElement`. A custom string is written as HTML, so untrusted content must be escaped by the caller |
| `enable`     | Always shown                   | Return `false` to skip that element                                                                                       |
| `offset`     | `[10, 10]`                     | Pixel offset from the pointer                                                                                             |
| `delay`      | `80`                           | Milliseconds to wait before a hover tooltip appears                                                                       |
| `className`  | `'g6lite-tooltip'`             | Overlay class name                                                                                                        |
| `container`  | `document.body`                | DOM node that hosts the overlay                                                                                           |

`getContent` receives a `TooltipContext` with `itemType`, `nodeId` or the edge's `edgeId` / `source` / `target`, `data`, and the original `event`.

Behavior combinations and events are in [Interactions](/en/docs/guides/interactions). A custom behavior uses [`register('behavior', ...)`](/en/docs/api/extensions).

## Theme [#theme]

```ts
theme?: 'light' | 'dark' | ({ type: 'light' | 'dark' } & Partial<ThemeTokens>)
```

An object starts from the preset named by `type`, then overrides tokens on that object. Overridable tokens are `nodeFill`, `nodeSize`, `nodeStroke`, `nodeStrokeWidth`, `edgeStroke`, `edgeLineWidth`, `edgeArrow`, `canvasBackground`, `edgeDefaultColor`, `edgeCategoryPalette`, `nodeStateStyles`, and `edgeStateStyles`.

```ts
import { resolveTheme } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const tokens = resolveTheme({ type: 'light', nodeFill: '#1677ff' });
```

`resolveTheme()` returns a new complete `ThemeTokens` and does not mutate the preset.

## Plugins and transforms [#plugins-and-transforms]

```ts
plugins?: Array<{ type: string; [option: string]: unknown }>
transforms?: Array<'process-parallel-edges' | string | { type: string; options?: object }>
```

A custom `plugins` or `transforms` `type` must be registered with `register()` first. The built-in transform name is `'process-parallel-edges'`.


# API stability and release boundary (/en/docs/compatibility/api-stability)



G6Lite remains in the `0.1.x` beta. The npm package root and `package.json#exports` define the only public API boundary. Do not import deep `src/` or build-output paths.

Recommended public entries include `Graph`, `register()`, `extensionFactory()`, `runLayout()`, and the configuration/data/extension types exported from the package root.

## ESM and CommonJS [#esm-and-commonjs]

The package root is ESM-only and does not provide a `require('@antv/g6-lite')` condition. A CommonJS feasibility test confirmed that a synchronous entry and declarations can be emitted, but a dual package must also preserve two runtime contracts:

* ESM and CommonJS consumers must share one extension registry when both formats are loaded by the same application.
* After application bundling, `layout.worker: true` must still resolve and load the package's module Worker instead of silently falling back to the main thread.

The current CommonJS consumer build cannot reliably preserve that Worker asset relationship and requests a missing Worker file; independent dual builds also create separate module-scoped registries. This release therefore does not publish a partial CommonJS build whose synchronous import works while Worker or extension behavior differs.

Applications that still use a CommonJS toolchain can cross the client boundary with dynamic import:

```js
const { Graph } = await import('@antv/g6-lite');
```

This does not change the requirement for a real DOM, Canvas, and WebGL environment.

Deprecated compatibility APIs include `BaseNode`, `BreathingNode`, `registerNode()`, `context.graph`, flattened ExtensionContext coordinate methods, `Graph#getAllData()`, and the old event `originalEvent` field. New code should use functional extensions, structured context, explicit queries, and current event objects.

Combo collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping remain experimental. The calls, methods, and option fields application code can use are documented in [Usable APIs](/en/docs/api), [Graph](/en/docs/api/graph), and [Options](/en/docs/api/options). Read the [Changelog](/en/docs/changelog) before upgrades and run type, build, and critical example checks.


# Browsers and runtime environment (/en/docs/compatibility/browser)



G6Lite prefers WebGL 2.0 and falls back to WebGL 1.0. Canvas 2D is used for labels and combo outlines, so WebGL 2.0 is not a hard requirement.

## Minimum versions [#minimum-versions]

| Browser                  | Minimum        | Release year | Main boundary                                     |
| ------------------------ | -------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Chrome                   | 80+            | 2020         | ES2020 syntax, native ESM, and WebGL 1.0          |
| Firefox                  | 74+            | 2020         | ES2020 syntax, native ESM, and WebGL 1.0          |
| Safari on macOS          | 13.1+          | 2020         | ES2020 syntax and WebGL 1.0                       |
| Safari on iOS            | 13.4+          | 2020         | ES2020 syntax; mobile GPU limits still apply      |
| Edge                     | 80+ (Chromium) | 2020         | Chromium-based Edge only; EdgeHTML is unsupported |
| Android WebView / Chrome | 80+            | 2020         | ES2020 syntax; validate low-end GPU capacity      |

Internet Explorer and EdgeHTML are not supported. These are syntax and platform boundaries for the untranspiled ESM-only package, not a complete certified device matrix. See [Can I Use optional chaining](https://caniuse.com/mdn-javascript_operators_optional_chaining), [Chrome 80](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/new-in-chrome-80), [Firefox 74](https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/74.0/releasenotes/), and [Safari 13.1](https://webkit.org/blog/10247/new-webkit-features-in-safari-13-1/).

## Coverage reference [#coverage-reference]

Using global usage data from `caniuse-lite@1.0.30001806`, retrieved on **2026-07-29**:

* The browser families and minimum versions explicitly listed above account for approximately &#x2A;*90.4%** of global browser usage.
* Across every browser tracked by Can I Use, versions supporting both WebGL 1.0 and native ESM account for approximately &#x2A;*94.8%**.

Sources: [Can I Use WebGL](https://caniuse.com/webgl), [JavaScript modules](https://caniuse.com/es6-module), and [caniuse-lite](https://github.com/browserslist/caniuse-lite). These figures are selection references, not G6Lite device certification rates. Enterprise browsers, embedded WebViews, disabled GPU acceleration, and low-end devices require separate validation.

## Comparison with sigma.js [#comparison-with-sigmajs]

The sigma.js v3 README describes a WebGL renderer for graphs with thousands of nodes and edges, built on Graphology. Its `sigma@3.0.3` package provides both ESM and CommonJS builds. The official [README](https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js#readme) and [package metadata](https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js/blob/main/packages/sigma/package.json) checked on 2026-07-29 do not publish an equivalent minimum-browser matrix.

An omitted matrix should not be interpreted as legacy-browser support. Both libraries require WebGL and a modern JavaScript toolchain; G6Lite explicitly documents the syntax floor of its untranspiled package, while sigma.js consumers need to validate their own build target.

G6Lite needs a real DOM canvas and WebGL context. In Next.js, Nuxt, or other SSR frameworks, instantiate `Graph` only on the client. Standard mini-program runtimes without compatible DOM and WebGL surfaces are not supported.

The renderer uses `regl`, which dynamically compiles WebGL commands. If the host enables Content Security Policy, `script-src` must allow `'unsafe-eval'`; `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` alone is not sufficient. Hosts that cannot allow this directive are not supported by the current renderer.

Hardware acceleration, mobile GPU memory, high DPR, and browser limits on active WebGL contexts affect capacity. Handle `WebGL not supported`, keep graph containers at non-zero size, and test realistic devices.


# Migrate from G6 v5 (/en/docs/compatibility/g6-v5-migration)



G6Lite keeps several G6 configuration concepts, but it is not a compatibility build of `@antv/g6` and does not promise source-compatible options or instance methods. This page compares `@antv/g6@5.1.1` with `@antv/g6-lite@0.1.0-beta.22`, checked on **2026-08-03**.

## Decide whether to migrate [#decide-whether-to-migrate]

A strong candidate normally meets all of these conditions: target browsers reliably support WebGL; the bottleneck is picking, state, and batch updates after rendering a large graph; the product mainly uses circle/rect nodes, common edges, labels, combos, and core interaction; and the team can accept the API stability boundary of a `0.1.x` beta.

Do not migrate directly when the application depends on G6 v5 multiple renderers, Node.js server rendering, React nodes, 3D, general animation orchestration, the mature plugin catalog, graph algorithms, or many arbitrary Canvas/SVG scene-graph shapes. Read the [graph library comparison](/en/docs/compatibility/library-comparison) and run both implementations on real data first.

## Installation and imports [#installation-and-imports]

```bash
npm install @antv/g6-lite
```

```ts
// G6 v5
import { Graph, NodeEvent } from '@antv/g6';

// G6Lite: consume the package-root public API only
import { Graph, register, extensionFactory } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import type { GraphData, GraphEventMap, GraphOptions } from '@antv/g6-lite';
```

Do not replace `@antv/g6/lib/...` imports with G6Lite `src/...` paths. The G6Lite public contract is limited to `package.json#exports` and package-root exports.

## Minimal configuration side by side [#minimal-configuration-side-by-side]

G6 v5:

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'container',
  data: {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'a', data: { label: 'A' } },
      { id: 'b', data: { label: 'B' } },
    ],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  node: {
    type: 'circle',
    style: {
      size: 24,
      fill: '#1783FF',
      labelText: (datum) => String(datum.data?.label ?? datum.id),
    },
  },
  edge: { type: 'line', style: { stroke: '#B8C2D1', endArrow: true } },
  layout: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 },
  behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-element', 'click-select'],
});

await graph.render();
```

Equivalent G6Lite starting point:

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'container',
  data: {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'a', data: { label: 'A' } },
      { id: 'b', data: { label: 'B' } },
    ],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  node: {
    type: 'circle',
    style: {
      size: 24,
      fill: '#1783FF',
      label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
    },
  },
  edge: { type: 'line', style: { stroke: '#B8C2D1', endArrow: true } },
  layout: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 },
  behaviors: [
    { type: 'zoom-canvas', sensitivity: 1, minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20 },
    'drag-canvas',
    'drag-node',
    'click-select',
  ],
});

await graph.render();
```

The immediate differences are `labelText` becoming `label`, `drag-element` becoming `drag-node`, and every node, edge, and extension style field needing validation against G6Lite package-root types.

## GraphOptions mapping [#graphoptions-mapping]

| Option                    | G6 v5                            | G6Lite migration                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container`               | String or container              | String or `HTMLElement`                                                                              |
| `data`                    | nodes / edges / combos           | Same concepts, but G6Lite requires `nodes` and `edges` arrays to exist                               |
| `node` / `edge` / `combo` | Full element configuration       | All supported, but types, style fields, and extension mechanisms are not field-compatible            |
| `layout`                  | Built-in and custom layouts      | 14 built-ins plus registered layouts; validate algorithm options individually                        |
| `behaviors`               | Behavior names or objects        | Strings or objects; names and options are mapped below                                               |
| `transforms`              | Built-in and custom Transforms   | `process-parallel-edges` and registered Transforms are supported with a different lifecycle contract |
| `plugins`                 | Rich built-in and custom plugins | Registered Plugin lifecycle is supported; built-ins and ecosystem are currently smaller              |
| `theme`                   | Theme and palette system         | `light` / `dark` plus a limited `ThemeTokens` override surface; fields differ                        |
| `animation`               | General animation configuration  | No equivalent GraphOptions animation system                                                          |
| `width` / `height`        | Constructor options and resize   | Container-driven; use `graph.setSize(width, height)` at runtime                                      |
| renderer                  | Canvas / SVG / WebGL and others  | Fixed hybrid path: WebGL for nodes/edges, Canvas 2D for labels/combos                                |

`graph.updateOptions()` currently updates `node`, `edge`, and `theme` only. Do not assume G6 v5 `setOptions()` semantics for replacing Behaviors, Plugins, Transforms, or Layout. Use `setLayout()` for layouts and rebuild or update Graph through the documented lifecycle for other configuration changes.

## Data field mapping [#data-field-mapping]

| G6 v5 field              | G6Lite                                 | Notes                                                                                |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GraphData.nodes`        | `GraphData.nodes`                      | Required; pass `[]` when empty                                                       |
| `GraphData.edges`        | `GraphData.edges`                      | Required                                                                             |
| `GraphData.combos`       | `GraphData.combos?`                    | Supported, but collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping remain experimental in beta |
| `node.id`                | `node.id`                              | Required and unique                                                                  |
| `node.data`              | `node.data`                            | Store business fields here; do not rely on G6 v5 internal model fields               |
| `node.style`             | `options.node.style`                   | Move shared styles to GraphOptions and use functions for per-node mapping            |
| `node.states`            | `node.states`                          | Initial states are supported; mutate with runtime state APIs                         |
| `node.combo` / `comboId` | `node.comboId`                         | Normalize to `comboId`                                                               |
| `node.x` / `node.y`      | Same names                             | Initial coordinates when layout is omitted                                           |
| `edge.id`                | `edge.id?`                             | Keep a stable explicit id for state and update APIs                                  |
| `edge.source` / `target` | Same names                             | Must reference existing node ids                                                     |
| `edge.data`              | `edge.data`                            | Business fields consumed by functional style mapping                                 |
| `combo.parentId`         | `combo.parentId`                       | Defines nested combos                                                                |
| `combo.style`            | `combo.style` or `options.combo.style` | Per-combo overrides and global configuration are both supported                      |

Nodes in the initial `GraphData` may omit coordinates when a layout is configured. Runtime `addNode()` requires `x` and `y`; migrate bulk creation to one `setData()` plus layout, or calculate coordinates before calling `addNode(s)`.

## Node, Edge, and Combo configuration [#node-edge-and-combo-configuration]

G6Lite builds in `circle` and `rect` nodes and `line`, `arc`, `polyline`, and `cubic` edges. `NodeConfig.type` and `EdgeConfig.type` also accept registered names, but custom extensions reuse built-in WebGL primitives and overlays rather than arbitrary G6 scene-graph shape trees.

Common mappings:

* Node text: migrate G6 v5 `labelText` to G6Lite `node.style.label`.
* Node size: use `size` for circles; rectangles can use `width`, `height`, and `borderRadius`.
* Edge arrows: use `startArrow`, `endArrow`, and `arrowSize`.
* Edge curves: do not copy quadratic and other type names blindly; choose `arc`, `cubic`, or `polyline` and configure `curvature`, `curveOffset`, `radius`, or `router`.
* Labels: node and edge labels support backgrounds, font styling, and placement; register a `label` extension for complex drawing instead of reaching into internal Canvas layers.
* State styles: use `node.stateStyles` and `edge.stateStyles`; combo state styles live under `combo.style.stateStyles`.
* Parallel edges: enable `edge.parallelEdges` or the `process-parallel-edges` Transform.

Combo declaration, nesting, collapse, runtime regrouping, states, and group drag are supported. See [Combo](/en/docs/guides/combo) and discard older migration notes that claimed G6Lite had no Combo support.

## Behavior mapping [#behavior-mapping]

| Common G6 v5 Behavior | G6Lite                | Migration note                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zoom-canvas`         | `zoom-canvas`         | Same name and G6-style delta-percentage `sensitivity`; G6Lite also batches per frame and caps each frame at 15%   |
| `drag-canvas`         | `drag-canvas`         | Same name; enabled with zoom when behaviors is omitted                                                            |
| `drag-element`        | `drag-node`           | Drags nodes and also drags a hit Combo as a group                                                                 |
| `click-select`        | `click-select`        | Single/multi-select options are supported; rebind payload types                                                   |
| `hover-activate`      | `hover-highlight`     | `highlight-node` and `highlight-edge` are also available                                                          |
| `brush-select`        | `brush-select`        | Shift/ctrl trigger options are supported                                                                          |
| `lasso-select`        | `lasso-select`        | Shift/ctrl trigger options are supported                                                                          |
| `collapse-expand`     | No same-name Behavior | Call `collapseCombo()`, `expandCombo()`, or `toggleCombo()`, or register an application Behavior                  |
| `create-edge`         | No direct equivalent  | `drag-edge` reconnects existing endpoints only; create a new edge in application interaction and call `addEdge()` |
| `focus-element`       | No same-name Behavior | Call `focusItem()` from the application event handler                                                             |
| `shortcuts-call`      | No same-name Behavior | Use the application shortcut layer or a custom Behavior                                                           |

The current 11 built-ins are `zoom-canvas`, `drag-canvas`, `highlight-node`, `highlight-edge`, `hover-highlight`, `drag-node`, `click-select`, `drag-edge`, `brush-select`, `lasso-select`, and `tooltip`.

When `behaviors` is omitted entirely, G6Lite enables `zoom-canvas` and `drag-canvas`. Passing `behaviors: []` disables those defaults. This differs from migration code that treats an empty list as “use defaults.”

## Layout migration [#layout-migration]

G6Lite currently supports `force`, `d3-force`, `force-atlas2`, `fruchterman`, `circular`, `concentric`, `radial`, `grid`, `dagre`, `mds`, `random`, `mindmap`, `indented`, and `fishbone`.

```ts
graph.setLayout({ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 40, ranksep: 80 });
await graph.layout();

// Starting another layout or destroying Graph also cancels the old run.
graph.cancelLayout();
```
